sources.title: Alibaba Cloud Model Studio model pricing — indexed Prime row
sources.evidence: Search-indexed page text (crawl reported five days before review) explicitly lists qwen3.8-max-prime under Qwen-Max, links it to Fast mode (Prime), and specifies thinking/non-thinking modes and an input pricing band through 1M tokens. The live fetched page omits that row; this is last-documented evidence, not proof of current endpoint operation.

sources.title: Alibaba Cloud Model Studio: Fast mode
sources.evidence: Page updated October 11, 2026 describes Fast mode as an API serving mode with 1.5–2x standard output TPS, token billing and separate model identifiers. Current supported-model table contains GLM and Wan entries, not Qwen3.8-Max-Prime. It does not identify the Prime Qwen checkpoint or state weight equivalence.

sources.title: qwen3.8-max Model Info
sources.evidence: Describes Qwen3.8-Max as a 2.4-trillion-parameter MoE model, documents image/text/video input, text output, function calling, thinking and a 1,000,000-token context. Lists qwen3.8-max-0902 (alias qwen3.8-max-2026-09-02) as an upgraded snapshot. No Prime identifier or Prime-to-snapshot mapping appears.

sources.title: Qwen3.8-Max: A New Bar for Coding and Cowork
sources.evidence: August 3, 2026 announcement publishes 2.4T total and 95B active for Qwen3.8-Max, based on the Qwen3.5 architecture. It contains benchmark tables for Max and announces forthcoming open weights. It does not mention Prime or the later 0902 snapshot.

sources.title: Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B official model card
sources.evidence: Separately released text checkpoint has a language-model count of 2.4T total/95B activated and hybrid Gated DeltaNet/Gated Attention with MoE. The card says hosted Qwen3.8-Max is based on this checkpoint with additional vision, non-thinking and service features. It does not equate the complete hosted Prime model with this checkpoint.

sources.title: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next official model card and benchmark tables
sources.evidence: Later first-party card and parameter comparison tables were checked for a Prime-specific disclosure. The table compares Flash-Next, 27B, Qwen3.7-Plus and external models; it supplies no Prime count or checkpoint mapping.

sources.title: Model lifecycle and updates
sources.evidence: Current October 22, 2026 page dates Qwen3.8-Max-0902 to September 2 and describes it as an upgraded snapshot of Max. Searches of the complete fetched English and Chinese lifecycle pages found no qwen3.8-max-prime release entry; neither page establishes Prime’s initial release date.

sources.title: OpenRouter live Qwen3.8 Max Prime endpoint metadata
sources.evidence: Direct HTTPS JSON read succeeds. Exact Prime ID has one Alibaba endpoint, a 1,000,000-token context, text/image/video input and text output, plus reasoning and tools parameters. Description identifies a higher-throughput Max SKU. created=1790191228 is 2026-09-23 19:20:28 UTC. This is first-party provider-interface evidence and a provider-listing timestamp; it supplies no network architecture, parameter count, license, or exact upstream snapshot mapping. No inference request was made.

sources.title: Models.dev Qwen3.8 Max Prime source record
sources.evidence: Baseline source cites Vercel and OpenRouter as accessed September 24, carries release_date September 23, and describes a high-throughput SKU. It is a catalog lead rather than independent technical verification.

sources.title: Qwen 3.8 Max Prime — Vercel AI Gateway
sources.evidence: Provider description says Prime retains Max’s 2.4T MoE architecture and capabilities, and lists September 23, 2026. These are useful leads, but no linked Alibaba statement establishes Prime’s weights or exact 0902 mapping; the technical claim is not promoted to developer-confirmed evidence.

sources.title: Prime 模式 — Chinese developer documentation
sources.evidence: Direct HTML inspection verifies the Chinese page states that supported capabilities and usage limits are the same as the original model (模型支持的能力、使用限制与原版模型相同). Its current supported-model table still omits Qwen3.8-Max-Prime. This supports the general serving-mode interpretation but does not state identical weights, a Prime parameter count or a Prime-to-0902 mapping.

name.note: Display normalization of the exact qwen3.8-max-prime service identifier.

developer.note: Alibaba pricing lists the SKU and live provider metadata attributes it to Alibaba’s Qwen team.

family.note: Prime is listed under Qwen-Max and described as a higher-throughput Qwen3.8 Max SKU. Family membership does not establish a particular checkpoint.

release_date.note: September 23 is confirmed only as the OpenRouter listing creation date and repeated by Vercel/catalogs. No Alibaba Prime release entry establishing the earliest public availability was found. Do not substitute Max’s August 3 launch or 0902’s September 2 date.

open_weights.note: Prime is documented as a hosted serving SKU. The public Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B checkpoint is not demonstrated to be the exact Prime weights; no explicit developer statement about the exact Prime checkpoint’s weight availability was located. Clear the categorical baseline assertion pending exact mapping.

license.note: No standalone weight license is documented for Prime. The separately published Qwen3.8-Max license for 2.4T-A95B cannot be assigned to Prime without an exact weight mapping; API service terms are not a weight license.

parameters_b.note: Alibaba discloses nominal 2400B for Max and the separate open checkpoint, but does not directly specify Prime or establish its precise checkpoint identity. Vercel’s inherited 2.4T claim is provider evidence, not original developer confirmation. Keep null; no complete or component count can safely be transferred.

active_parameters_b.note: Nominal 95B is explicit for launch Max and the open language checkpoint. Prime-to-Max/0902 identity is unresolved, so 95B is not copied. This is a verification gap for this variant, not a claim that the family’s active count is wholly undisclosed.

architecture.note: Primary Max specification says MoE and the separate open checkpoint specifies its hybrid attention stack. Neither explicitly maps that network to Prime. Serving-mode identity is supported, while exact independent-weight or shared-checkpoint identity remains unresolved. The Chinese Prime documentation states that capabilities and usage limits match the original model; it does not establish identical weights or name the Qwen snapshot.

context_window.note: The live Alibaba endpoint metadata on OpenRouter explicitly reports 1,000,000 context tokens. This verifies the provider-documented interface limit, not a generation test.

modalities.note: Live exact-endpoint metadata documents these input and output modalities. No modality is inherited solely from the standard Max record.

reasoning.note: Alibaba’s indexed Prime pricing row includes thinking mode, and the exact live endpoint supports reasoning parameters.

tool_call.note: Live exact endpoint exposes tools and tool_choice; auto and none are supported. This is provider-interface documentation, not a tool-execution test.

description.value: Fast mode API variant of Qwen3.8 Max with a one-million-token context and text, image and video input.
description.note: Use a service-level description; omit unverified independent-model implications and inherited performance claims.

patch.description: Fast mode API variant of Qwen3.8 Max with a one-million-token context and text, image and video input.
patch.notes: Prime is documented as a fast API serving SKU. Exact Prime-to-Max/0902 checkpoint mapping is unverified; Max’s nominal 2.4T/95B counts and open-checkpoint license are not transferred. September 23, 2026 is the verified OpenRouter listing date, not a confirmed earliest public release. Current Alibaba fetched pages omit the Prime row retained in indexed pricing text. Interface capabilities are verified from live OpenRouter metadata for its Alibaba endpoint, without inference testing.

sources.label: Alibaba Prime pricing (indexed row; current page differs)

summary: Prime is an API serving mode/SKU within Qwen3.8 Max. Exact Prime-to-Max/0902 weight identity was not established by primary developer evidence, so total/active counts and architecture remain null; the later Flash-Next benchmark table provides no missing bridge. Confirmed exact provider interface: 1M context, text/image/video to text, reasoning and tools. Clear unsupported earliest release day and categorical open-weight assertion; preserve September 23 as provider-listing metadata in notes. Unresolved exact mapping prevents assigning Max’s counts or the separate checkpoint license.
